pages.title: Axiom of Choice
pages.text: Given any collection of non-empty sets, you may choose one element from each, even when no rule tells you which. It seems harmless, yet it implies that a sphere can be cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two spheres. The token feels decisive.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to choose a point from each piece of the continuum and it could not without an extra axiom. I wrote one in and it immediately proved Banach-Tarski.
